reason: The cited evidence does not address FeNiCrCoCu or pre-annealing effects on its wear resistance. E1 describes inverse Hall-Petch and amorphization in CoCrFeMnNi, not microstructural refinement by annealing. E2 shows hardness increase after 500°C annealing in CoCrFeNiMn coatings due to nanotwins and dislocations, but provides no wear or deformation data and concerns a different alloy. Thus, the key premises linking annealing to refined microstructure and improved high-temperature wear resistance lack direct support.
premises: Pre-annealing FeNiCrCoCu induces a refined near-surface microstructure (nanoprecipitates, segregation, or twins).
This refined microstructure impedes dislocation motion and grain boundary sliding during high-temperature sliding.
Impeded dislocation motion and grain boundary sliding reduce microscopic plastic deformation and wear rate.
The effect is operative under high-temperature sliding (400–600°C) in low-oxidation environments.
